transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-05-13 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya, Liam (Redwood); Sara, Diego, Nina (Halcyon)

Summary (auto): procurement kickoff focusing on legal redlines, SLA selection, and technical onboarding.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in today. quick run of who we are, and then liam will walk the tech bits, and we can get into the MSA/DPA points Sara outlined.
[00:18] Sara (Halcyon - Procurement): thanks Maya. we wanted to get alignment on the legal path and timelines, also Diego has a few infosec blockers we need to confirm before procurement can greenlight.
[00:27] Diego (InfoSec): yep main ones are: SOC2 Type II, support for customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM), audit logs retention, and any data residency options. also we need clarity on egress fees and network topology for private deployments.
[00:41] Liam (Redwood SE): great — on the tech side we support three modes: hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private (VPC or on-prem). for BYOK we integrate with KMS and can provide HSM-backed key custody in Private mode, and for Dedicated there are options for customer key wraps.
[01:05] Nina (Vendor Ops): quick Q — if we go private, do we still get the same SLA? our legal needs uptime and 95th percentile latency for inference.
[01:15] Maya: yes — SLA tiers carry across modes. our 99.95% uptime tier includes latency SLOs measured at per-route 95th percentile; we can propose a 95p < 200ms baseline for the pilot, depends on model & sequence length.
[01:34] Sara: whoops sorry can you repeat the latency number?
[01:36] Liam: 200 milliseconds at the 95th, that is a typical target for smaller models / shorter sequences. for larger gen workloads it shifts; we note that in the perf profiles.
[01:50] Diego: and credits? what is the remediation if SLA misses? need those in the agreement.
[01:56] Maya: standard SLA credits in the MSA — service credits back to account; we can surface that language in the MSA redline. we'll highlight the SLA credit thresholds and measurement windows in the workbook.
[02:10] Speaker 1: um and pricing, we discussed per-token vs reserved — which is more cost-effective for steady production?
[02:18] Maya: Reserved/dedicated works best for predictable throughput; we can provide committed monthly capacity with a unit price lower than hosted pay-as-you-go. there is also burst capacity option. we'll attach a pricing matrix.
[02:33] Diego: we have a compliance question on the DPA: clause 5.2 around subprocessor location — we need stronger data residency commitments. is that possible?
[02:42] Liam: we can offer region pinning on Private and Dedicated, and in Hosted we have region controls too; we'll call that out in the DPA redline. sometimes the transcriber shows region names oddly — but yes, we can pin to eu-west-1 and do contractual commitments.
[03:00] Sara: timeline: procurement wants to finish legal review within two weeks if possible. is that realistic?
[03:06] Maya: yes, if we get DPA redlines today and we push SOC2 and artifacts, 1-2 weeks is typical. we'll need to expedite with our legal ops; I'll flag it.
[03:15] Diego: on key custody — we require HSM-backed BYOK for production workloads. do you support HSM vs KMS? wording sometimes says K M S which confuses people.
[03:26] Liam: yes we support both. for Private deployments we can integrate with customer HSM via KMIP or cloud-HSM; for Hosted we have bring-your-own-key integrations with supported cloud KMS providers, and we can do a managed HSM offering as add-on.
[03:44] Nina: any additional onboarding costs for private?
[03:47] Maya: Private has a platform fee and onboarding engineering hours; we usually itemize professional services in the SOW. for many customers, starting with Dedicated pilot then moving to Private is the lower friction path.
[04:00] Sara: procurement will need to see SOW estimate + a skeleton invoice for internal approvals.
[04:05] Maya: will provide an initial SOW template and estimated fees in the pricing packet.
[04:12] [04:12] Liam: quick tech note — network: for VPC peering we require 443 outbound allowed to a set of IP ranges, and we provide a connectivity checklist; we also support S2S VPN for airgapped setups. egress fees are billed based on cloud egress in private/dedicated and we can show a model for expected egress costs.
[04:35] Diego: egress is big for us — our models often send longer context; can we negotiate egress into the committed capacity?
[04:42] Maya: we can model that in the pricing runbook; for large commitments we can amortize egress or provide a blended rate. I'll flag that for pricing.
[04:55] Speaker 2: on auditing — how long are logs retained, and can we export them to our SIEM?
[05:02] Liam: audit logs are retained per plan; we support exporting logs via S3 or direct ingestion to major SIEMs. default retention is 90 days, extended retention available as add-on.
[05:15] Diego: need 365 day retention for certain logs for compliance — can you confirm export + archive support?
[05:21] Liam: yes we can set up archival pipelines to your S3 and keep them for 1+ years. we'll put that in the runbook.
[05:28] Maya: quick check on DPA redlines — Sara, you mentioned one non-negotiable earlier?
[05:32] Sara: correct — we want a clause on incident notification windows (48 hours) and a promise to provide forensic artifacts.
[05:40] Maya: standard is 72 hours for incidents, but for enterprise we can move to 48 hours in the DPA and include forensic support language; I'll mark that as a redline we can push.
[05:48] Nina: procurement will also ask about insurance and breach liability caps.
[05:52] Maya: yes we have vendor insurance details; we'll include limits and provide certificates.
[05:57] [08:12] Liam: jumping back to performance — for the pilot we'd recommend a small reserved pool attached to the app routes you plan to exercise. pilot targets: 95p latency <200ms, throughput 250 reqs/min sustained, and cost target X per 1M tokens (we'll detail the numbers in the pricing sheet).
[08:32] Diego: can we run an E2E bench? we want to validate latency from our VPC to the runtime.
[08:38] Liam: absolutely — we'll schedule a run after the connectivity session. needs about 2 hours of setup time and a short test harness.
[08:45] Maya: ok so immediate next steps: send SOC2 + DPA redline; schedule connectivity runbook; share pricing matrix. any other must-haves?
[08:56] Sara: procurement needs named approvers. I'll email the list after.
[09:01] Diego: also need a point on data deletion and purge timelines.
[09:06] Maya: our data retention & deletion policy is in the security packet; we also support per-customer retention controls in Private mode.
[09:15] Speaker 3: little bit of cross-talk about who owns the KV cache — transcription noted KV cash earlier — but to confirm who owns cached prefixes?
[09:24] Liam: good question — by default caching is managed by the service to optimize perf; for Private or Dedicated we offer optional customer-managed caches to meet data control needs.
[09:40] Nina: how do rollouts work — can we do canary and automatic fallback to smaller models on overload?
[09:46] Liam: yes our platform supports route-level rollouts, canary percentage, and automatic fallback to lower tier model variants if capacity constrained. we'll include that in the ops runbook.
[09:58] Diego: from legal — we will likely ask for a clause that prohibits Redwood from using customer data for model training.
[10:05] Maya: we have that as a standard in the DPA — no training on customer data unless explicitly allowed. we'll highlight that clause for you.
[10:13] Sara: timeframe: procurement review by 5/21, pilot start window 5/25-6/1, decision by 6/10. can you commit to that?
[10:21] Maya: yes we'll align internal resources.
[10:27] [20:02] Liam: one more technical nuance — KMS integrations vary by cloud. if you use on-prem HSM we'll need to validate latency for signing operations — typically negligible but we should include test cases.
[20:18] Diego: noted. also want to understand fallbacks — if we lose a region, what does the failover look like for private?
[20:25] Liam: Private is customer-run so failover is within customer ops; for Dedicated/Hosted we have automated multi-region routing and can failover to a partner region. we'll document RTO/RPO expectations.
[20:40] Nina: procurement asks: do we need sub-processors approval for certain vendors?
[20:45] Maya: we list subprocessors in the DPA and can add a notification/approval step for critical subprocessors; this is a common ask.
[21:00] Diego: are there any known latency regressions with quantized models? sometimes the transcribed note says quantiz… quantizational but basically quantization can slightly change quality.
[21:10] Liam: yes quantization affects quality/latency tradeoffs — we recommend profiling prompts during pilot; Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization profiles per workload.
[21:22] Sara: ok thanks — this is helpful, please send documents.
[21:26] Maya: final recap: Maya will send SOC2 type II, security packet, and DPA redline by 5/18. Liam will send connectivity checklist and propose times for the VPC deep-dive / bench. Halcyon will confirm approvers and pricing preference by 5/21.
[21:43] Nina: thanks all, we'll review and come back with DPA comments.
[21:48] Maya: great — talk soon.

Notes: Shared artifacts referenced during call: pricing matrix (link: drive.redwood/pricing/halcyon-proposal.xlsx), security packet (link: drive.redwood/security/redwood-soc2-2025.pdf), connectivity checklist (link: drive.redwood/ops/vpc-checklist.pdf). The transcript includes typical auto-transcription errors (KV cash, K M S spelled out).

End of transcript.
